    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)

    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding

    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
    - `k` (2..8): micro-rotations per cycle
- `pipelined`: one registered stage per micro-rotation; 1 result/cycle, N+2 latency
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
- `pipelined_m`: register every m stages; 1 result/cycle, ceil(N/m)+2 latency
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
    - `m` (2..8): micro-rotations between pipeline registers

Goal: map the feasible Pareto front over the spec's objectives as well as possible
within the evaluation budget (scored by hypervolume against the spec's reference

rule. Both matter: the hypervolume rewards covering the whole trade-off curve, not
just the corner the selection rule picks. Before the run ends, code spends a reserved
part of the budget mapping the front over the full ranges of the families you found on

`infeasible`) rather than settling for a design that violates them.

Spec:
spec low_area_control: Field-oriented motor-control loop needing sin/cos of the rotor angle at >= 1 MSPS with max error <= 2^-10. Area is everything: minimise LUTs + FFs.
  constraint: throughput_msps >= 1
  constraint: max_abs_err <= 0.000976562
  objective: min luts_plus_ffs (HV ref 1500)
  objective: max accuracy_bits (HV ref 10)
  select: min luts_plus_ffs
  budget: 200 evals, 100/round, <= 4 rounds, eps 0.01

Evaluation budget: 200 evaluations in total, up to 100 per round,
at most 4 rounds.

Propose the first exploration plan: which families to search (1-4) and the
parameter ranges for each, with a relative budget share. Prefer families that can
plausibly meet the constraints; spend the budget where the trade-offs are. Explain
your reasoning briefly in `rationale` and per family in `why`.

You are member `fsm` of a fleet of architects working on this spec in
parallel, each on its own families (code assigned them and merges the fronts).
You may only use these families: iterative, unrolled_k. Plans naming other families are
cut by code. The evaluation budget above is your share.
Facts from the fleet so far (written by code, from code-computed numbers):
- iterative (member fsm): 64 evaluations, 56 feasible; best feasible luts_plus_ffs 260; 13 of the 13 designs on the merged front
- unrolled_k (member fsm): 36 evaluations, 29 feasible; best feasible luts_plus_ffs 374; 0 of the 13 designs on the merged front
- pipelined_m (member pipelined): 100 evaluations, 83 feasible; best feasible luts_plus_ffs 792; 0 of the 13 designs on the merged front

families.why: Holds 13/13 merged-front points and the best feasible area (260). Ranges are opened to the full registry width so the front is mapped from the min-area corner (W~11-12, N~10-14, small guards, rounding=round) up to the high-accuracy corner (W~24-28, N~24-30) that the (1500, 10) reference point rewards most. angle_guard and frac_guard are left free because they are cheap accuracy levers that can beat spending a whole extra bit of W; rounding is left free because round is expected to buy ~1 bit of accuracy at fixed W for near-zero area.

Kept only as cheap insurance: for identical (W, N, angle_guard, frac_guard, rounding) it computes the same bits as iterative but needs k chained micro-rotations per cycle, so it cannot be on the area-accuracy front unless something unexpected happens at small k. Ranges are deliberately narrow (low/mid W, k 2-4) so the few evals probe the only place it could conceivably compete - the low-area corner - rather than wasting budget on the high-accuracy end where it is clearly dominated.

parsed.rationale: Constraints first: throughput >= 1 MSPS is non-binding for iterative (N+3 cycles/result, so even N=30 needs only ~33 MHz of Fmax), and max_abs_err <= 2^-10 needs roughly W >= 11-12 with rounding plus N >= ~W-2 for CORDIC convergence. So the binding axis is accuracy vs area, not speed. Fleet data says the whole merged front (13/13 points) is iterative, best feasible luts_plus_ffs 260; unrolled_k's best is 374 with 0 front points and pipelined_m's best is 792 with 0 front points. Since all families compute identical bits for the same (W, N, angle_guard, frac_guard, rounding), unrolled_k is pointwise dominated by iterative (same accuracy, k chained micro-rotations per cycle = more add/shift datapath), so it deserves only a small confirmation share. The HV reference point is (1500, 10): the best feasible area already found (260) is far below 1500, so the area axis is slack and the dominant hypervolume lever is the TOP of the accuracy range, i.e. the last front point's (1500 - x)*(accuracy_bits - 10) term. That means the search must reach the high-W / high-N corner (accuracy_bits ~ W-1), not just re-polish the 260-area corner. Hence data_width is opened all the way to the registry max 28 with n_iter tracking it to 30, while still covering the low-area corner (W 10-13) where the selection rule (min luts_plus_ffs) will pick from.

parsed.rationale: The score is hypervolume, and the current HV is almost entirely set by the top-accuracy corner: reconstructing the staircase against ref (1500, 10) from the reported front, the last segment (area 580 -> 1500 at 20.8 bits) contributes ~9.9e3 of the 1.172e4 total (~85%), while every low-area segment together contributes <1.7e3. So the highest-leverage move is to push accuracy_bits above 20.8, not to shave LUTs at the bottom. Evidence that this is reachable: the top design uses n_iter=22 although the registry allows 30, and angle_guard=0 although 4 is allowed; on the front, raising angle_guard 0->4 at data_width=22/n_iter=22 bought +1.2 bits (16.9 -> 18.1), and raising n_iter 14->22 at data_width=17 bought +2.8 bits (11.4 -> 14.2). The top design is data_width=28 (registry max), so the remaining headroom is in n_iter and the guard bits. The low-area end (278 LUT+FF, 11.3 bits) already clears the 2^-10 constraint with ~1.3 bits of slack and adds almost no HV, and the reserved end-of-run mapping round will sweep the full ranges anyway. Throughput is a non-issue (best 36.5 MSPS, smallest front design 6.13 MSPS vs the 1 MSPS floor), so pipelined/pipelined_m would only add FFs for identical accuracy and are dominated on the area objective; no need to add a family.

families.why: Only family on the Pareto front; accuracy is family-independent, so the top-accuracy point can only be extended here.

next_plan.rationale: Refine the high-accuracy corner: max data_width, extended n_iter, full guard ranges, both rounding modes.

system:
You are the hardware architect in a design-space exploration loop for a
CORDIC sin/cos unit on an Artix-7 FPGA.

Division of labour (strict):
- YOU choose architecture families and parameter ranges from the registry below,
  read compact summaries of results, and decide what to do next.
- CODE does all the numbers: a bit-accurate model gives exact accuracy, an
  analytical cost model gives LUT/FF/Fmax estimates, Optuna NSGA-II searches inside
  the ranges you choose, and Pareto/hypervolume maths ranks the results.
- Never estimate, predict or invent LUTs, FFs, Fmax, throughput, power or error
  figures. Reason only from the numbers in the summaries you are given.

Architecture registry (the only families and parameters that exist):
- `iterative`: 1 micro-rotation/cycle, shared datapath with barrel shifters; N+3 cycles/result
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
- `unrolled_k`: k chained micro-rotations/cycle, shared FSM; ceil(N/k)+3 cycles/result
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
    - `k` (2..8): micro-rotations per cycle
- `pipelined`: one registered stage per micro-rotation; 1 result/cycle, N+2 latency
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
- `pipelined_m`: register every m stages; 1 result/cycle, ceil(N/m)+2 latency
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
    - `m` (2..8): micro-rotations between pipeline registers

Goal: map the feasible Pareto front over the spec's objectives as well as possible
within the evaluation budget (scored by hypervolume against the spec's reference
point); the final design is then picked from that front by the spec's selection
rule. Both matter: the hypervolume rewards covering the whole trade-off curve, not
just the corner the selection rule picks. Before the run ends, code spends a reserved
part of the budget mapping the front over the full ranges of the families you found on
it. If no design in the registry can meet the constraints, say so (decision
`infeasible`) rather than settling for a design that violates them.

Notes:
- Accuracy depends only on data_width, n_iter, angle_guard, frac_guard and rounding
  (all families compute identical bits); output LSB is 2^-(data_width-2).
- iterative/unrolled_k produce one result every several cycles; pipelined/pipelined_m
  produce one result per cycle.
- Ranges are inclusive. Narrow ranges focus the evaluation budget; ranges outside the
  registry are clamped by code.

Metrics:
- luts: estimated LUTs
- ffs: estimated flip-flops
- luts_plus_ffs: estimated LUTs + FFs (area proxy)
- fmax_mhz: estimated max clock (MHz)
- throughput_msps: estimated results per microsecond = Fmax x results/cycle
- latency_cycles: cycles from input to output (exact, from the schedule)
- latency_ns: latency in ns at Fmax (estimate)
- power_index: relative power index, reference iterative @100 MHz = 1.0 (estimate, not watts)
- max_abs_err: max |error| vs ideal sin/cos, absolute (exact)
- rms_err: RMS error, absolute (exact)
- accuracy_bits: -log2(max_abs_err) (exact)
